title: Inverse trigonometric values and trigonometric equations on an interval

stimulus.title: Inverse trigonometric values and equations
stimulus.text: No calculator. Give exact values, use radians, and show the work for each part. Only real solutions are asked for.

table.caption: The expressions and equations in this question, by part

parts.label: A(i)
parts.sample: $\sin\frac{7\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}$. Then $\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)$ is the angle in $[0, \pi]$ with cosine $-\frac{1}{2}$, which is $\frac{2\pi}{3}$.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.sample: Apply tangent to both sides: $2x - 1 = \tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1$. So $2x = 2$ and $x = 1$.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Solve $\sin(2x) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $0 \le x \le \pi$. Show the work that leads to your answers.

rubric.point: Works with $2x$ on the doubled interval $[0, 2\pi]$ and finds $2x = \frac{4\pi}{3}$ and $2x = \frac{5\pi}{3}$ (or one correct value of $x$)
Both solutions $x = \frac{2\pi}{3}$ and $x = \frac{5\pi}{6}$, and no others

parts.sample: Let $u = 2x$. For $0 \le x \le \pi$, $0 \le u \le 2\pi$. $\sin u = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ in Quadrants III and IV with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$: $u = \frac{4\pi}{3}$ or $u = \frac{5\pi}{3}$. Divide by $2$: $x = \frac{2\pi}{3}$ or $x = \frac{5\pi}{6}$.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Solve $2\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0$ for $0 \le x < 2\pi$. Show the work that leads to your answers.

rubric.point: Factors (or uses the quadratic formula) to get $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin x = -1$
All three solutions $x = \frac{\pi}{6}$, $\frac{5\pi}{6}$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, and no others

parts.sample: Treat $\sin x$ as the variable: $(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1) = 0$. So $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$, giving $x = \frac{\pi}{6}$ and $x = \frac{5\pi}{6}$, or $\sin x = -1$, giving $x = \frac{3\pi}{2}$. The solutions are $\frac{\pi}{6}$, $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{3\pi}{2}$.
